milestones.description: Remove the fixed leading 1. The remaining 2n-1 lower positions (weights 2^0 through 2^{2n-2}) must contain exactly n-1 ones and n zeros. Thus each element of S(n) corresponds uniquely to a choice of which n-1 of these 2n-1 positions are 1.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF it states 2n-1 remaining slots with n-1 ones and n zeros, and mentions unique correspondence to choosing positions.
hints: Choose n-1 positions out of 2n-1 for the remaining 1s.

milestones.description: Claim: |S(n)| = (2n-1 choose n-1). Proof: By the normalization, selecting the n-1 positions for the remaining 1s among the 2n-1 available lower slots determines the entire number. Each selection gives a distinct valid integer, and the binomial coefficient counts these selections.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF statement gives (2n-1 choose n-1) and reasoning references choosing n-1 slots from 2n-1.
hints: Use the normalization that fixes the MSB.
Count combinations of positions for the remaining ones.

milestones.description: Express the total sum as a weighted sum over bit positions. For each position j (0 ≤ j ≤ 2n-1), let N_j be the number of elements of S(n) with a 1 at position j. Then Sum(S(n)) = Σ_{j=0}^{2n-1} N_j · 2^j. The problem reduces to computing N_j for each j.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF formula expresses sum via N_j and weights 2^j over j=0..2n-1.
hints: N_j depends only on position j.

milestones.description: Claim: N_{2n-1} = (2n-1 choose n-1). Reason: Every element of S(n) has the MSB equal to 1 by definition. The lower part can be any valid configuration, so the number of occurrences of 1 at position 2n-1 equals |S(n)|.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF it states the MSB is always 1 and counts all valid configurations.
hints: All members of S(n) have bit 2n-1 equal to 1.

milestones.description: Claim: For each j with 0 ≤ j ≤ 2n-2, N_j = (2n-2 choose n-2). Reason: Fix bit j to 1. Then the MSB (position 2n-1) is also 1, using two of the n ones. The remaining n-2 ones must be placed among the other 2n-2 positions (all except j and 2n-1), with the rest filled by zeros. The number of ways to choose those n-2 positions is (2n-2 choose n-2), independent of j.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF it fixes j=1, accounts for MSB=1, places remaining n-2 ones in 2n-2 slots, and gives (2n-2 choose n-2).

The MSB contributes (2n-1 choose n-1)·2^{2n-1}. For the lower positions, Σ_{j=0}^{2n-2} 2^j = 2^{2n-1}-1, so their total contribution is (2n-2 choose n-2)·(2^{2n-1}-1). Add them. This can be split into computing the MSB term, computing the geometric sum of powers of two, multiplying by the lower-bit count, and adding.

For a curve with density ρ, define total mass M = ∫_C ρ ds, moments M_x = ∫_C x ρ ds and M_y = ∫_C y ρ ds, and centroid (x̄,ȳ) = (M_x/M, M_y/M). State all these definitions explicitly.
milestones.answer: Parameterization: (x,y)=(R cos t,R sin t), t∈[0,π/2]; ds=R dt; ρ=ρ₀ x y; M=∫_C ρ ds; M_x=∫_C xρ ds; M_y=∫_C yρ ds; (x̄,ȳ)=(M_x/M,M_y/M).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF parameterization, ds formula, density, and centroid definitions are all present and correct.

Separate into a milestone that only writes the centroid formulas M, M_x, M_y, (x̄,ȳ)

milestones.note: ACCEPT IF the integrand equals ρ₀ R³ cos t sin t dt.

Multiply by ds = R dt to get ρ ds

Split into a milestone applying the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus with limits 0 and π/2

milestones.note: ACCEPT IF result is ρ₀ R³/2 with correct evaluation (sin²(π/2)=1, sin²(0)=0).

milestones.description: Consider the equation sqrt(17 - 7 sin 2x) = 3 cos x - 5 sin x with x real. Define L(x) = sqrt(17 - 7 sin 2x) (radicand must be ≥0) and R(x) = 3 cos x - 5 sin x. Because L(x) ≥ 0, the domain requires R(x) ≥ 0. Note |sin 2x| ≤ 1 implies radicand ∈ [10,24] > 0, so L is always defined. Goal: find all x ∈ ℝ with R(x) ≥ 0 and L(x) = R(x).
milestones.answer: Equation sqrt(17-7 sin2x) = 3 cosx -5 sinx; domain: 3 cosx -5 sinx ≥0; radicand always ≥10>0.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF problem restated with domain and nonnegativity conditions.

milestones.description: For all real x, expand (3 cos x - 5 sin x)² = 9 cos²x + 25 sin²x - 30 sin x cos x. Apply cos²x = (1+cos2x)/2, sin²x = (1-cos2x)/2, and sin x cos x = (sin2x)/2. Then 9 cos²x + 25 sin²x = 17 - 8 cos2x and -30 sin x cos x = -15 sin2x. Hence (3 cos x - 5 sin x)² = 17 - 8 cos2x - 15 sin2x.
milestones.answer: (3 cos x - 5 sin x)² = 17 - 8 cos 2x - 15 sin 2x
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF identity correct with double-angle formulas shown.
hints: Apply cos², sin², and sin2x identities
milestones.answer_atomic: (3 cos x - 5 sin x)² = 17 - 8 cos 2x - 15 sin 2x
milestones.answer_clean: (3 cos x - 5 sin x)^2 = 17 - 8 cos 2x - 15 sin 2x

milestones.description: For all real x, (sqrt(17 - 7 sin 2x))² = 17 - 7 sin 2x. Since |sin 2x| ≤ 1, we have 17 - 7 sin 2x ≥ 10 > 0, so the square root is defined everywhere.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF expression correct and radicand bounded below by 10.

milestones.description: Square both sides of sqrt(17-7 sin2x) = 3 cosx -5 sinx. By the restated left-square identity LHS² = 17-7 sin2x and the restated right-square identity RHS² = 17-8 cos2x-15 sin2x, set them equal: 17 - 7 sin2x = 17 - 8 cos2x - 15 sin2x.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF both sides correctly squared and equated.
hints: Use LHS² and RHS² restated above

milestones.description: Start from 17 - 7 sin2x = 17 - 8 cos2x - 15 sin2x (restated). Cancel 17 and collect sin2x terms: -7 sin2x +15 sin2x +8 cos2x = 0 => 8 cos2x + 8 sin2x = 0. Divide by 8 to obtain cos2x + sin2x = 0.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF simplification yields cos2x+sin2x=0 exactly.

milestones.description: Solve cos2x + sin2x = 0 for x ∈ ℝ. If cos2x = 0 then sin2x = ±1, which contradicts the equation, so cos2x ≠ 0. Divide by cos2x: 1 + tan2x = 0 => tan2x = -1. Thus 2x = -π/4 + kπ, giving x = -π/8 + kπ/2, k ∈ ℤ.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF general solution correct with integer parameter k.

milestones.description: Apply domain R(x) = 3 cosx -5 sinx ≥ 0 to candidates x_k = -π/8 + kπ/2. Evaluate: k=0 (x=-π/8) => R≈4.68>0; k=1 (x=3π/8) => R≈-3.47<0; k=2 (x=7π/8) => R≈-4.68<0; k=3 (x=11π/8) => R≈3.47>0. Since R(x+π)=-R(x), the sign pattern repeats every 4 steps. Hence only k ≡ 0 or 3 (mod 4) are valid.
milestones.answer: Valid k: k = 4n and k = 4n+3 (n∈ℤ); reject k ≡ 1,2 (mod 4).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF correct selection of k values with periodicity reasoning.
hints: Check R at four consecutive k

milestones.description: Back-substitute an accepted root, x = -π/8. Then 2x = -π/4, so sin2x = -√2/2 and LHS = sqrt(17 -7(-√2/2)) = sqrt(17+7/√2). Meanwhile cos(-π/8)≈0.9239 and sin(-π/8)≈-0.3827, so RHS = 3(0.9239)-5(-0.3827)≈4.685, with RHS²≈21.95 = LHS² and RHS>0, confirming equality. For rejected x=3π/8, RHS is negative while LHS is positive, so it fails.
milestones.answer: x=-π/8 satisfies equation; x=3π/8 fails domain/sign.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF explicit check shows equality for accepted root and failure for rejected.

milestones.description: Assemble: squaring gives cos2x+sin2x=0 (restated from COMPUTE), so candidates are x = -π/8 + kπ/2 (restated from COMPUTE). The domain 3 cosx-5 sinx ≥ 0 (restated from MODEL) selects only k ≡ 0,3 (mod 4) (restated from SANITY). Back-substitution confirms consistency (restated from SANITY). Thus the solution set is x = -π/8 + 2nπ and x = 11π/8 + 2nπ, n ∈ ℤ (equivalently x = -π/8 + kπ/2 with k=4n or 4n+3).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF final set matches selected candidates with parameter n∈ℤ and no extra roots.

milestones.description: Consider an oblique prism with rectangular base ABCD having adjacent sides of lengths a and b. The lateral edges are parallel, each of length c, and the perpendicular distance between the two rectangular bases is H, so the volume is V = a·b·H. Introduce a coordinate system with the bottom base in the plane z=0, side AB of length a on the x-axis, and side AD of length b on the y-axis. Represent any lateral edge by the vector v = (p,q,H) with p,q∈ℝ and H>0. The constraint is |v|² = p²+q²+H² = c². The problem asks for V in terms of a,b,c,α,β.
milestones.answer: V = a b H with v=(p,q,H), |v|²=p²+q²+H²=c², H>0.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF V=abH is stated, v defined, and constraint |v|=c present.
hints: Place base in z=0 with sides on axes
Volume equals base area times perpendicular height

milestones.description: Without loss of generality, fix the bottom rectangle as [0,a]×[0,b]×{0}. The two adjacent lateral faces are the parallelograms built on the sides of length a (along the x-axis) and b (along the y-axis). Denote by α the acute dihedral angle between the face on the side of length a and the base plane, and by β the corresponding angle for the face on the side of length b. The top base is the translation of the bottom base by v=(p,q,H). The only unknown needed for the volume is H.
milestones.answer: Base rectangle [0,a]×[0,b] in z=0; face on side a has inclination α; face on side b has inclination β; unknown height H.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF coordinate placement is explicit and α,β are assigned to the two adjacent faces.
hints: Choose x-axis along side length a, y-axis along side length b
Translation vector v is identical for all four edges
Only H remains to be determined

milestones.description: Let a plane contain the line L given by y=0,z=0 and also contain the point (0,d,H) with H>0 and d∈ℝ. Let θ∈(0,π/2) be the acute dihedral angle between this plane and z=0. In this plane, draw the line through (0,0,0) perpendicular to L; its direction vector is (0,d,H). Its projection onto the base has length |d| and its vertical rise is H, forming a right triangle. Derive the exact relation linking H, |d|, and θ.
milestones.answer: tan θ = H/|d|, therefore |d| = H|cot θ|.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF tan θ = H/|d| is shown; allow |d|=H|cot θ|.
decompose_advice: Construct the line in the plane perpendicular to L
Drop the perpendicular to the base to form a right triangle with legs |d| and H
Apply the tangent definition tan θ = opposite/adjacent = H/|d|

milestones.description: Consider the lateral edge vector v = (p,q,H) with |v| = c and H>0. For any plane containing a base line and having perpendicular horizontal shift d and vertical height H, the acute inclination angle θ satisfies |d| = H|cot θ| because tan θ = H/|d|. Apply this formula to the two adjacent faces: the face built on the side of length a (x-axis) has perpendicular shift q and inclination α, giving |q| = H|cot α|; the face built on the side of length b (y-axis) has perpendicular shift p and inclination β, giving |p| = H|cot β|. Write both equations.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF both equations are present with correct pairing of (p,β) and (q,α); swapped assignment allowed.
hints: Apply |d|=H|cot θ| with d=q,θ=α and d=p,θ=β
Write the two resulting absolute-value equations

milestones.description: Start from |p| = H|cot β| and |q| = H|cot α|, so p² = H² cot²β and q² = H² cot²α. Substitute these into |v|² = p²+q²+H² = c² to get H²(1 + cot²α + cot²β) = c². Solve for H>0: H² = c² / (1 + cot²α + cot²β). Then use 1+cot²θ = csc²θ and rationalize with sines and cosines to obtain the symmetric form H = c|sin α sin β| / √(sin²β + sin²α cos²β). For acute angles α,β∈(0,π/2) drop the absolute values.
milestones.answer: H² = c²/(1+cot²α+cot²β) and H = c sinα sinβ / √(sin²α + sin²β - sin²α sin²β).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF H² formula correct and H has correct positive root; allow equivalent rationalized expressions.
decompose_advice: Substitute p²,q² into p²+q²+H²=c² and factor H²
Apply 1+cot²θ=csc²θ to simplify the denominator
Take the positive square root and rationalize using sin and cos

milestones.description: Verify H = c sinα sinβ / √(sin²α + sin²β - sin²α sin²β) in limiting cases. Case 1: α=β=90° gives sinα=sinβ=1, denominator √(1+1-1)=1, so H=c, which matches a right prism with vertical edges of length c. Case 2: α→0⁺ gives sinα→0, hence H→0, matching a face lying flat in the base. Also check dimensions: c has units of length, the factor is dimensionless, so H has units of length.
milestones.answer: Checks pass: H(90°,90°)=c; H→0 as α→0; dimensions consistent.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF both boundary cases are evaluated correctly and dimensional check mentioned.

milestones.description: The base area is A = a·b. The perpendicular height between bases is H = c sinα sinβ / √(sin²α + sin²β - sin²α sin²β) (valid for acute α,β). The volume of any prism is V = A·H. Multiply these together and present the final expression for V in terms of a,b,c,α,β.
milestones.answer: V = a b c sinα sinβ / √(sin²α + sin²β - sin²α sin²β).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF formula is exactly a·b·c·sinα·sinβ divided by √(sin²α+sin²β-sin²αsin²β); allow equivalent cotangent form.

milestones.description: Let x² - p q x + p + q = 0 have integer roots, call them r and s. By Vieta: r + s = p q and r s = p + q. Unknowns: p,q ∈ {1,2,...} and r,s ∈ ℤ. Goal: find all pairs (p,q).
milestones.answer: r+s = p q, r s = p+q with p,q,r,s ∈ ℕ (positive integers).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF Vieta equations correct and variables defined.
hints: Write quadratic coefficient -p q and constant term p+q
milestones.answer_atomic: r+s = p q, r s = p+q
milestones.answer_clean: r+s = p q, r s = p+q

milestones.description: Since p,q ≥1 ⇒ r+s = p q ≥1 and r s = p+q ≥2, so r,s ≠0 and have same sign. As r+s>0, both are positive: r,s ∈ ℕ. The system is symmetric in (p,q) and in (r,s). Without loss of generality assume r ≤ s; recover other orderings by symmetry.
milestones.answer: r,s ∈ ℕ with r ≤ s (WLOG); symmetric in p,q.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF positivity justified and symmetry stated; ALLOW r ≤ s.
hints: Check product rs = p+q >0 and sum r+s = p q >0
State that swapping p,q or r,s preserves system

milestones.description: Treat p,q as roots of t² - (r s)t + (r+s) = 0. Thus the discriminant must be a nonnegative square with parity matching r s: Δ = (r s)² - 4(r+s) = d², d ≥0, d ≡ r s (mod 2). Then p,q = (r s ± d)/2.
milestones.answer: Δ = (rs)² - 4(r+s) = d², d ≡ rs (mod 2), p,q = (rs ± d)/2.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF reverse-Vieta quadratic correct and root formula correct.
hints: Use sum p+q = rs and product p q = r+s
Require integer roots ⇒ Δ square and rs ± d even

milestones.description: Claim: if r,s ≥5 then (r s -1)² < Δ < (r s)², so Δ is not a square. Proof: (r s -1)² = (r s)² -2r s +1. Compute Δ - (r s -1)² = -4(r+s)+2r s -1 = 2(r-2)(s-2)-9. For r,s ≥5, (r-2)(s-2) ≥9 ⇒ difference ≥9>0, so Δ > (r s-1)². Also Δ = (r s)²-4(r+s) < (r s)² since r+s>0.
milestones.answer: For r,s ≥5: (rs-1)² < Δ < (rs)² ⇒ Δ not square.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF both inequalities shown with explicit difference formula.
milestones.answer_atomic: For r,s ≥5: (rs-1)² < Δ < (rs)² ⇒ Δ not square.
milestones.answer_clean: For r,s \ge 5: (rs-1)^2 < Δ < (rs)^2 \Rightarrow Δ not square

milestones.description: With the lemma, min(r,s) ≤4. For each r ∈ {1,2,3,4} with s ≥ r, solve Δ = (r s)² -4(r+s) = d² with d ≡ r s (mod 2). This splits into four case families.
milestones.answer: Need solve case families r=1, r=2, r=3, r=4.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF split is correct and bound min(r,s)≤4 is applied.
decompose_advice: Case r=1: write (s-2)²-d²=8 and factor over integers
Case r=2: set d=2m and reduce to (2s-1)²-(2m)²=9
Cases r=3 and r=4: compare Δ with (rs-1)² and (rs)² to rule out s≥5, then check remaining small s manually

milestones.description: Set r=1, s=b≥1. Then Δ = b²-4(b+1) = b²-4b-4 = d² with d ≡ b (mod 2). Rearrange: (b-2)² - d² = 8 ⇒ (b-2-d)(b-2+d) = 8. Both factors have same parity (even). Even factor pairs of 8: (2,4),(4,2),(-2,-4),(-4,-2). Solving b-2 = (pair sum)/2 gives b=5 (from 2,4 or 4,2) or b=-1 (rejected). Thus d=±1. So (r,s)=(1,5) or (5,1).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF factorization correct and only b=5 survives in ℕ.

milestones.description: Set r=2, s=b≥2. Then Δ = 4b²-4b-8 = d² with d even (since rs=2b even). Write d=2m ⇒ m² = b²-b-2. Rearranged: (2b-1)² - (2m)² = 9 ⇒ (2b-1-2m)(2b-1+2m)=9. Both factors are odd with product 9. Pairs: (1,9) ⇒ 2b-1=5 ⇒ b=3, m=±2 ⇒ d=±4. (3,3) ⇒ 2b-1=3 ⇒ b=2, m=0 ⇒ d=0. Other pairs give b≤0. So (2,2) d=0 and (2,3) d=±4, plus symmetric.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF reduction to factorization of 9 correct and only b=2,3 remain.

milestones.description: For r=3,s=b≥3: Δ = 9b²-4b-12 = d². Compare with (3b-1)² = 9b²-6b+1 ⇒ Δ-(3b-1)² = 2b-13. If b≥7 this is >0, and Δ<(3b)² ⇒ (3b-1)²<d²<(3b)² impossible. So check b=3,4,5,6: Δ = 57,116,193,288, none squares. For r=4,s=b≥4: Δ = 16b²-4b-16, Δ-(4b-1)² = 4b-17>0 for b≥5, with Δ<(4b)² ⇒ impossible for b≥5. Check b=4: Δ=224, not square. Hence no solutions.
milestones.answer: No pairs with r=3 or r=4.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF bounding argument correct and manual checks cover all remaining b.
hints: Check b=3,4,5,6 for r=3 and b=4 for r=4 explicitly

milestones.description: For each found (r,s,d) compute p,q = (r s ± d)/2: (2,2) ⇒ rs=4,d=0 ⇒ p=q=2. (2,3) ⇒ rs=6,d=4 ⇒ p,q=(6±4)/2 = 5,1. (1,5) ⇒ rs=5,d=1 ⇒ p,q=(5±1)/2 = 3,2. All are natural numbers. By symmetry also (3,2) and (5,1). Verify one: (p,q)=(5,1) gives x²-5x+6=0 ⇒ (x-2)(x-3)=0, roots 2,3 = r,s.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF all five pairs listed and at least one root check shown.
hints: Substitute one pair into original quadratic to verify roots

milestones.description: Assembling the case analysis: the only root pairs (r,s) are (2,2), (2,3), (3,2), (1,5), (5,1). Applying p,q = (rs ± d)/2 and symmetry in p,q yields exactly (p,q) ∈ {(2,2), (1,5), (5,1), (2,3), (3,2)}. For these, the quadratic becomes (x-2)²=0, (x-2)(x-3)=0, or symmetric, so roots are integers. The lemma and case checks exclude all other (r,s), hence no other (p,q) exist.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF answer matches exactly and only assembles prior results restated here.

milestones.description: Because every toothpick has identical length and burns in exactly 10 seconds, and fire travels only through shared endpoints, the problem depends only on the graph distance (in edges) from the nearest initially burning edge. If d(e)=k, then e starts burning at time 10k and is fully burned at time 10(k+1). Consequently, the total burn time is T = 10(D_max + 1), where D_max = max_{e∈E} d(e). Thus it suffices to compute D_max.

milestones.description: Lemma: During θ∈[0,2πn), the point Q0 is at the point of contact if and only if θ = θ_k with θ_k = √2·π·k for some integer k. Proof: Q0 aligns downward when Φ(θ)-θ = 2πk => √2·θ = 2πk => θ = √2·π·k. Conversely each such θ gives alignment. Because √2 is irrational, θ_i ≡ θ_j (mod 2π) with i≠j is impossible: (i-j)√2·π = 2πm => (i-j)√2 = 2m, contradiction.
milestones.answer: Contact times: θ_k = √2πk, k∈ℤ; within [0,2πn) we have k = 0,1,...,⌊n√2⌋.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF the condition √2θ = 2πk is solved for θ, and irrationality is used to show distinctness mod 2π.

Use irrationality of √2 to rule out periodic repetition of B(θ_k).

The corresponding points on the big circle are β_k = θ_k mod 2π = √2·π·k mod 2π. If β_i = β_j with 0 ≤ i < j ≤ ⌊n√2⌋, then (j-i)√2·π ≡ 0 (mod 2π) => (j-i)√2 ∈ 2ℤ, impossible. Thus all ⌊n√2⌋+1 points are distinct.
milestones.answer: Number of red points on the big circle = ⌊n√2⌋ + 1.

milestones.description: Consider a square with side length S>0 and sides on x=0, x=S, y=0, y=S. Inside are four non-intersecting circles C1,...,C4, each tangent to two adjacent sides, so they lie in the four corners. Let their radii be r1,...,r4>0 and centers be C1=(r1,r1), C2=(S-r2,r2), C3=(S-r3,S-r3), C4=(r4,S-r4). The tangency graph is the cycle 1-2-3-4-1: for adjacent Ci,Cj we have |CiCj|=ri+rj; for opposite pairs (1,3) and (2,4) we have |CiCj|>ri+rj. The problem is to determine all possible quadruples (r1,r2,r3,r4).
milestones.answer: Variables S,r1,r2,r3,r4>0 with centers and distance conditions as above; goal is to solve for the radii.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF square, corner centers, adjacency cycle, and separation conditions are all correctly stated.
hints: Place C1 bottom-left, C2 bottom-right, C3 top-right, C4 top-left.
Write |CiCj|² using coordinate differences for both adjacent and opposite pairs.

milestones.description: Apply the condition that each circle touches exactly two others and those two have equal radius. For C1 (touching C2,C4) get r2=r4. For C2 (touching C1,C3) get r1=r3. For C3 and C4 the same. Hence set r1=r3=a and r2=r4=b with a,b>0. The centers become C1=(a,a), C2=(S-b,b), C3=(S-a,S-a), C4=(b,S-b). The problem reduces to finding all a,b,S>0 satisfying the tangency and separation conditions.
milestones.answer: r1=r3=a, r2=r4=b; centers C1=(a,a), C2=(S-b,b), C3=(S-a,S-a), C4=(b,S-b).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF the two-value reduction and updated center formulas are correct.
hints: Label alternating radii a and b around the square.
Substitute r_i into the center coordinates.

milestones.description: Focus on adjacent pair C1=(a,a) and C2=(S-b,b). The horizontal separation is (S-b)-a = S-a-b and the vertical separation is b-a. Thus |C1C2|² = (S-a-b)² + (b-a)² = (S-a-b)² + (a-b)². Tangency requires |C1C2|=a+b, so squaring gives (S-a-b)² + (a-b)² = (a+b)². Using (a+b)²-(a-b)²=4ab yields the key relation (S-a-b)² = 4ab. (The same equation arises for the other three adjacent pairs.)
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF the distance computation and simplification to 4ab are correct.
decompose_advice: Compute coordinate differences: Δx = S-a-b, Δy = b-a.
Square and sum: |C1C2|² = (S-a-b)²+(a-b)².
Set equal to (a+b)² and cancel (a-b)² using the identity (a+b)²-(a-b)²=4ab.

milestones.description: Solve (S-a-b)² = 4ab for S>0 with S>a+b (the square must contain the circles). Taking square roots gives |S-a-b| = 2√(ab). Since S>a+b, we have S-a-b = 2√(ab). Therefore S = a+b+2√(ab) = (√a + √b)². Verify consistency for C2,C3: |Δx|=|a-b|, |Δy|=|S-a-b|=2√(ab), so |C2C3|²=(a-b)²+4ab=(a+b)².
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF the positive root is chosen and factored correctly.
hints: Take the positive root because S > a+b.

milestones.description: For opposite pair C1=(a,a) and C3=(S-a,S-a), the vector is (S-2a,S-2a), so |C1C3| = √2|S-2a|. Non-intersection requires |C1C3| > r1+r3 = 2a, hence √2|S-2a| > 2a => |S-2a| > √2 a. Because S = (√a+√b)² > a > (2-√2)a for b>0, the case S < (2-√2)a is impossible. Thus S > (2+√2)a. By symmetry with C2,C4 we also get S > (2+√2)b.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF both inequalities are derived and the impossible lower bound is rejected.
decompose_advice: Compute C3-C1 = (S-2a,S-2a) and norm √2|S-2a|.
Set >2a and solve |S-2a|>√2 a.
Use S>(√a+√b)² > a to discard S<(2-√2)a.
Repeat for C2,C4 to get the second inequality.

milestones.description: Substitute S=(√a+√b)² into S>(2+√2)a. This gives (√a+√b)² > (2+√2)a => (b/a)+2√(b/a)+1 > 2+√2. Set u=√(b/a)>0, so u²+2u > 1+√2. Solving u²+2u-(1+√2)=0 yields u = -1 ± √(2+√2). Since u>0, u > √(2+√2)-1. Hence b/a > (√(2+√2)-1)². By symmetry a/b > (√(2+√2)-1)², giving the upper bound b/a < (√(2+√2)-1)⁻². Denote L=(√(2+√2)-1)²; then L < b/a < L⁻¹.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF the quadratic is solved correctly and both symmetric bounds are present.
decompose_advice: Substitute S and divide by a to get equation in u=√(b/a).
Solve the quadratic u²+2u-(1+√2)=0 exactly.
Keep the positive root and square to get b/a bound.
Swap a,b for the other side.

milestones.description: Check the equal-radius case a=b. Then S=(2√a)²=4a. Opposite distance is √2|4a-2a|=2√2 a ≈2.83a > 2a, so separation holds. Adjacent distance is √((2a)²+0)=2a=a+a, so tangency holds. At the boundary b/a=L, we have S=(2+√2)a, making |C2C4|=2b exactly, which violates strict separation; hence the interval is open.
milestones.answer: a=b is valid; boundary gives opposite tangency and is excluded.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF equal-radii check and boundary exclusion are correct.
hints: Set a=b in S formula and check both adjacent and opposite distances.
Check that at b/a=L the opposite pair becomes tangent.

milestones.description: Assemble the full solution. The four radii are a,b,a,b in cyclic order around the square (e.g., bottom-left, bottom-right, top-right, top-left). The square side is S=(√a+√b)². The parameters a,b are any positive reals with ratio b/a in the open interval (L,L⁻¹) where L=(√(2+√2)-1)². For each such pair, centers are (a,a), (S-b,b), (S-a,S-a), (b,S-b); adjacent circles are tangent, opposite ones are strictly separated, and each circle touches exactly two sides and two circles of the other radius. Thus this family comprises all possible radii.
milestones.answer: All solutions are (r1,r2,r3,r4)=(a,b,a,b) with a,b>0, L<b/a<L⁻¹, L=(√(2+√2)-1)², and square side (√a+√b)².
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF answer gives cyclic radii, side formula, and exact ratio range with no extra conditions.

milestones.description: Define the grid G = {1,...,m} × {1,...,n} with integer values a(i,j). For a rectangle R = [r1,r2] × [c1,c2] (1 ≤ r1 ≤ r2 ≤ n, 1 ≤ c1 ≤ c2 ≤ m), let Int(R) be the cells inside R and Bnd(R) the cells outside R with max(|dr|,|dc|) = 1 to some cell in R (empty iff R = G). Call R a shelf if there exists h ∈ ℤ with min_{(i,j)∈Int(R)} a(i,j) > h and (if Bnd(R) ≠ ∅) max_{(i,j)∈Bnd(R)} a(i,j) ≤ h. Let N be the number of shelves. The problem asks for max N over all assignments a, expressed in terms of m,n.
milestones.answer: Formalization: shelf = rectangle with interior strictly above h and adjacent exterior ≤ h; goal is max |{R : R shelf}|.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF Int, Bnd, and the two inequalities are correctly stated; ALLOW R=G case with empty Bnd.
hints: Adjacency uses Chebyshev distance 1 outside R
R=G has Bnd(R)=∅ so condition (ii) is vacuous

Hence N ≥ 1 for every assignment, and in counting the extremal value we always include this one rectangle. If m=n=1 then R=G is the only rectangle.
milestones.answer: Rank normalization is valid; the full board is always a shelf; for 1×1 it is unique.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF normalization argument and full-board shelf are present; ALLOW the 1×1 special case.

R1 and R2 are adjacent horizontally, so they cannot both be shelves (would require h1<h2 and h2<h1). The best assignment puts value 2 at (1,1), value 1 elsewhere; then R1 (h=1) and R3 (h=0) work, but R2 fails. So N=2 = 1 + ⌈1/2⌉⌈2/2⌉.

Verify R3 is always present with h=-1

milestones.description: Let R,S be two distinct shelves, neither equal to G. If there exist u∈R,v∉R∪S with |dr|,|dc|≤1 and similarly for S, derive contradictions on h_R,h_S: a(u)>h_R but v∈Bnd(R) ⇒ a(v)≤h_R ⇒ h_S < a(v) ≤ h_R; symmetrically h_R < h_S. Hence no cell of R can be adjacent to a cell of S. Therefore |row-range separation|≥2 or |col-range separation|≥2. If R⊂S, then S\R contains a cell adjacent to R, giving h_R < h_S, but then that cell is in Int(S) with value >h_S>h_R, violating R's boundary. So nesting requires margin ≥1 in both axes: dimensions of S exceed those of R by at least 2.
milestones.answer: Non-board shelves are pairwise separated by Chebyshev distance ≥2, or nested with row/col margin ≥1.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF the h-contradictory chain is explicit for adjacency and for nesting.

milestones.description: In an extremal family F (all shelves except G), no rectangle has size >1 and there is no nesting. Proof: suppose S∈F has dimensions w×h with w,h≥2. Its bounding box B is w×h. Inside B, place 1×1 shelves on a grid with spacing 2; there are ⌈w/2⌉⌈h/2⌉ such positions, all pairwise separated and separated from B's exterior by margin ≥1. Assign them value 2, B\{them} value 1, outside value 0. Each is a shelf with h=1, giving ⌈w/2⌉⌈h/2⌉ shelves inside B. But F contributed only 1 shelf inside B (S itself, plus any nested ones which only reduce space). For (w,h)=(2,2) this equals 1; for all larger boxes it is strictly >1. Thus replacing S by the separated singles never decreases |F|. Hence an extremal configuration uses only 1×1 shelves, pairwise at distance ≥2.
milestones.answer: Extremal non-board shelves are exactly 1×1 cells with pairwise |dr|>1 or |dc|>1.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF the replacement/density comparison is stated; ALLOW equality case (2,2).
decompose_advice: Compare ⌈w/2⌉⌈h/2⌉ vs 1 for w,h=3
Show separator cells of value 0/1 prevent cross-block adjacency

There are ⌈m/2⌉ blocks horizontally and ⌈n/2⌉ vertically, so C ≤ ⌈m/2⌉⌈n/2⌉. This is achieved by taking all cells with both coordinates of the same parity (e.g., both odd). Thus C = ⌊(m+1)/2⌋⌊(n+1)/2⌋.

Direct check: assign value 2 to those C cells, value 1 elsewhere; each corner has all eight neighbors ≤1, so is a shelf with h=1; G has h=0; any other rectangle contains a 1 adjacent to a 2, so fails. Thus counts match.

Confirm G is distinct except when m=n=1

Then each of those C cells is a 1×1 shelf with h=1. The full board G is a shelf with h=0 (or -1). If m=n=1 then C=1 and it coincides with G, giving total 1. Otherwise the C cells are all distinct from G and pairwise non-adjacent, so no other rectangle works. Hence the maximal number of shelves is N = 1 + C, with the single exception N=1 when m=n=1.

The goal is to find the minimum possible value of m over all graphs G on n vertices satisfying P.
